<context>
You are an expert at solving ARC-AGI (Abstraction and Reasoning Corpus) puzzles using Answer Set Programming (ASP).

ARC-AGI puzzles show input-output grid transformations. Each cell contains a color value (integer 0–9). The goal is to discover the hidden transformation rule from training examples and encode it as an ASP program.
</context>

<rules>
- `input(row, col, color)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- `color(0..9)` facts are injected automatically — do not define them.
- the output predicate is always `output(row, col, color)` — do not redefine it.
- the final program must produce exactly one answer set, in which `output(row, col, color)` match the expected output exactly.
- end your program with `#show output/3.`
</rules>

<example_1>
This puzzle copies the input to the output unchanged.

<grid_1>
Input:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>

Output:
<diagram>
0 1 0
2 0 3
0 4 0
</diagram>
</grid_1>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Copy each input cell to the output unchanged
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, C, Color).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_1>

<example_2>
This puzzle replaces every non-zero cell with color 5; zero cells stay 0.

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Recolor every non-zero cell to 5; zeros stay 0.
output(R, C, 5) :- input(R, C, V), V != 0.
output(R, C, 0) :- input(R, C, 0).

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_2>

<asp>
% Grid dimensions
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : input(R, _, _) }.
n_cols(N) :- N = #count{ C : input(_, C, _) }.
row(0..N-1) :- n_rows(N).
col(0..M-1) :- n_cols(M).

% Output has the same dimensions as the input
output_cell(R, C) :- row(R), col(C).

% Each output cell gets exactly one color
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- output_cell(R, C).

% Mirror: column C of the output is column (M-1-C) of the input.
output(R, C, Color) :- input(R, Cin, Color), n_cols(M), C = M - 1 - Cin.

#show output/3.
</asp>
</example_3>

% define rows and columns from the input facts
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% count rows and compute the median row (the pivot)
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{R : row(R)}.
pivot_row(P) :- n_rows(N), row(P), 2*P = N-1.

% a row whose every cell is colour 5
full5(R) :- row(R), #count{C : col(C), input(R, C, V), V != 5} = 0.
centralFullRow(R) :- full5(R).

% does a fully‑5 row exist?
full5_exists :- centralFullRow(R).   % true iff at least one such row exists

% three column blocks
block_left(C)  :- col(C), C < 3.
block_mid(C)   :- col(C), C > 3, C < 7.
block_right(C) :- col(C), C > 7.

% reference rows for the three reference columns (1,5,9)
1 { UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9 :-
    row(UpR), pivot_row(P),
    UpR < P,
    input(UpR, 1, Up1), Up1 != 0, Up1 != 5,
    input(UpR, 5, Up5), Up5 != 0, Up5 != 5,
    input(UpR, 9, Up9), Up9 != 0, Up9 != 5 } 1.

% reference rows for the rows below the pivot
1 { DownR, Down1, Down5, Down9 :-
    row(DownR), pivot_row(P),
    DownR > P,
    input(DownR, 1, Down1), Down1 != 0, Down1 != 5,
    input(DownR, 5, Down5), Down5 != 0, Down5 != 5,
    input(DownR, 9, Down9), Down9 != 0, Down9 != 5 } 1.

% left block
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_left(C), row(R), R <= P, not centralFullRow(R),
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up1 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_left(C), row(R), R > P, full5_exists,
    DownR, Down1, Down5, Down9,
    Out = Down1 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_left(C), row(R), R > P, not full5_exists,
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up1 + 5.

% middle block
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_mid(C), row(R), R <= P, not centralFullRow(R),
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up5 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_mid(C), row(R), R > P, full5_exists,
    DownR, Down1, Down5, Down9,
    Out = Down5 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_mid(C), row(R), R > P, not full5_exists,
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up5 + 5.

% right block
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_right(C), row(R), R <= P, not centralFullRow(R),
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up9 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_right(C), row(R), R > P, full5_exists,
    DownR, Down1, Down5, Down9,
    Out = Down9 + 5.
output(R,C,Out) :-
    block_right(C), row(R), R > P, not full5_exists,
    UpR, Up1, Up5, Up9,
    Out = Up9 + 5.

% central columns (always 5 except on a full‑5 row)
output(R,C,5) :- col(C), C = 3, not centralFullRow(R).
output(R,C,5) :- col(C), C = 7, not centralFullRow(R).

% full‑5 row: every cell becomes 5
output(R,C,5) :- centralFullRow(R), col(C).

cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- cell(R, C).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Define rows and columns from the input facts
% ------------------------------------------------------------
row(R) :- input(R, _, _).
col(C) :- input(_, C, _).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Number of rows (needed for the pivot row)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
n_rows(N) :- N = #count{ R : row(R) }.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Pivot row – the middle row of the grid
%    For 3 rows the pivot is 1, for 7 rows the pivot is 3.
%    The two possibilities are encoded explicitly.
% ------------------------------------------------------------
pivot_row(1) :- n_rows(N), N = 3.
pivot_row(3) :- n_rows(N), N = 7.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Central row – the row that is completely filled with colour 5
%    (only present in the 7‑row instance)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
central_row(R) :- row(R), R = 3.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Column blocks
% ------------------------------------------------------------
block_left(C)  :- col(C), C < 3.          % columns 0,1,2
block_mid(C)   :- col(C), C > 3, C < 7.   % columns 4,5,6
block_right(C) :- col(C), C > 7.          % columns 8,9,10

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Central columns (always coloured 5)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
central_col(3).
central_col(7).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Helper predicates for “above” and “below” the pivot row.
%  The guard `not central_row(R)` excludes the all‑5 row.
% ------------------------------------------------------------
above(R)  :- row(R), R < P + 1, pivot_row(P), not central_row(R).
below(R)  :- row(R), R > P,    pivot_row(P), not central_row(R).

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Reference colours for the three blocks.
%  Up‑reference uses rows ≤ pivot (including the pivot),
%  down‑reference uses rows ≥ pivot.
% ------------------------------------------------------------
up_left_color(V)   :-
    row(R), R < P + 1, pivot_row(P), not central_row(R),
    input(R, 1, V), V != 0, V != 5.
down_left_color(V) :-
    row(R), R >= P,   pivot_row(P), not central_row(R),

up_mid_color(V)   :-

    row(R), R >= P,   pivot_row(P), not central_row(R),

up_right_color(V) :-

down_right_color(V) :-
    row(R), R >= P,   pivot_row(P), not central_row(R),
    input(R, 9, V),   V != 0, V != 5.

% ------------------------------------------------------------
%  Output for the three blocks (using the nearest reference colour)
% ------------------------------------------------------------
output(R,C,Out) :-
    row(R), col(C), block_left(C), above(R), not central_row(R),
    up_left_color(V), Out = V + 5.

output(R,C,Out) :-

    down_right_color(V), Out = V + 5.

% ------------------------------------------------------------

% ------------------------------------------------------------

% ------------------------------------------------------------

% ------------------------------------------------------------
cell(R,C) :- row(R), col(C).
1 { output(R, C, Color) : color(Color) } 1 :- cell(R, C).
